item.text: {"results":[{"pair_id":"J01250","case1_error":"Evaluates the correctly written calorie sum as 2175 instead of 1975.","case2_error":"Averages only two younger sisters’ clothing, omitting Nicole from the required three-person average.","reason":"The first is arithmetic evaluation; the second uses an incorrect averaging population and denominator.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J01251","case1_error":"Uses 8/12 instead of Jill’s capacity divided by Jack’s current apples, 24/8.","case2_error":"Calculates only Jake’s consumption, omitting his brother’s and father’s consumption from the purchase requirement.","reason":"The first constructs the wrong ratio; the second omits consumers when calculating total demand.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J01252","case1_error":"Gives unsupported final answer 19 after outlining a procedure that would yield 17; no numerical calculation is shown.","case2_error":"Adds purchased chickens to dead chickens instead of surviving chickens.","reason":"The first supplies an unsupported final number; the second explicitly states an incorrect relation for the remaining flock.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J01253","case1_error":"Uses Jack’s current apples divided by Jack’s capacity instead of Jill’s capacity divided by Jack’s current apples.","case2_error":"Counts discount groups using five apples instead of all ten fruits.","reason":"The first chooses the wrong ratio and orientation; the second omits eligible items from the discount count.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J01254","case1_error":"Treats each smaller antacid as weighing 3 grams, although the question specifies 1 gram.","case2_error":"Incorrectly evaluates 86400 × 9.81 as 849144; the product is 847584.","reason":"The first substitutes an incorrect given weight; the second miscalculates a correctly written expression, regardless of the interpretation of weight.","judgment":"different"}]}
